features.name: Task runner over the 112, with resume
features.description:
Batch runner across REAL's task set, plus the supervisor that drives it unattended. MUST CHECKPOINT AND RESUME: the archived predecessor lost an eight-hour run that produced nothing because it could not resume after a failure. A task already completed is never re-run on resume, and the runner states how many it skipped. One task's failure never aborts the batch.

THE RULES ARE IN docs/DECISIONS.md ENTRY 7, decided before this feature exists because none of them can be applied honestly after seeing the results. Implement them, do not re-litigate them:
(a) runs/<run-id>/manifest.json is written before the first task and never edited — the task ids, the population they were drawn from (112 / 102 / 47, see entry 5), and every exclusion with its reason.
(b) One atomically-written record per task (tmp file + os.replace, so a kill mid-write cannot corrupt one). Terminal statuses: passed, failed, capped, errored. Each record carries reward, steps, tokens, wall-clock, and which cap fired if one did.
(c) A provider error (429, 401, entitlement change, reset) is NOT a task failure and NOT terminal — status provider_error, the task stays unattempted, and it is retryable. Recording provider errors as zero-reward failures is how an unattended run publishes a wrong success rate.
(d) runs/<run-id>/results.tsv is append-only, one row per ATTEMPT including retries. The rate is computed from each task's FIRST terminal attempt; retries exist to survive interruptions, never to re-roll a task until it passes.
(e) scripts/supervise.py re-invokes the runner until one of three machine-checkable outcomes and never runs unbounded: exit 0 every manifest task terminal; exit 1 stalled, K consecutive rounds added no new terminal record; exit 2 token or wall-clock budget exceeded. Idempotent — re-running after a completed run prints the summary and changes nothing. Each round logs what it attempted, what became terminal, and any backoff.

(f) CONCURRENCY, per entry 7's second half: --concurrency N, DEFAULT 3, because z.ai publishes a per-model concurrency limit and for glm-4.6 it is 3. This machine (10 cores, 64 GB) is not the constraint — an episode is model-bound, 9 model calls over 35 s in the gate. Workers are PROCESSES, not threads: agisdk drives Playwright's sync API, which has thread affinity. No two concurrent episodes on the same site until state isolation is measured — REAL scores by diffing environment state, and a shared server-side site would contaminate both diffs. A concurrency-limit rejection is a provider_error under (c), never a task failure, and the supervisor halves concurrency on one and recovers slowly. The manifest records the concurrency level, because per-task wall-clock at N=3 is not comparable to sequential.

BEFORE THE FULL RUN: the published limit of 3 is for the pay-as-you-go API and this key is a Coding Plan key — probe 2, 3, 4 and 5 concurrent trivial completions, record which are rejected and with what code, and write the measured number into docs/DECISIONS.md. Do NOT switch to glm-4.5 or glm-5.1 for their higher limits; that changes the subject of the measurement and is a human decision.

SCOPE: no worktree isolation, no separate methodology file (AGENTS.md and these fields are it), and no model in the supervision path — the evaluator is agisdk's programmatic checks.
